body:
### Motivation
- Evitar `AmbiguousForeignKeysError` de SQLAlchemy al tener múltiples FK hacia `users.id` en modelos como `Order`, `Remito`, `StockMovement`, `MermaEvent`, etc. 
- Registrar eventos de auditoría y soportar el flujo de `inventory counts` (creación, envío, aprobación, cierre, cancelación) en backend y frontend. 
- Mantener nombres consistentes para las relaciones hacia `User` y no romper la API pública. 

### Description
- Se añadieron `sa_relationship_kwargs={"foreign_keys": "[Model.column]"}` en relaciones hacia `User` para `Order.cancelled_by_user`, `Order.created_by_user`, `Order.updated_by_user`, `Remito.created_by_user`, `Remito.updated_by_user`, `StockMovement.created_by_user`, `MermaEvent.reported_by_user`, y en las relaciones inversas en `User` para `reported_mermas` y `audit_logs` para eliminar ambigüedad. 
- Se introdujo el modelo `AuditLog` y los modelos `InventoryCount` / `InventoryCountItem` con sus FKs y relaciones, y se añadieron los enums `AuditAction` e `InventoryCountStatus` en `common.py`. 
- Se extendió `api/routes.py` con utilidades de auditoría (`_encode_changes`, `_log_audit`), mappers para mostrar nombres de usuarios, endpoints CRUD y de estado para `/inventory-counts` y `/audit/logs`, y se añadieron llamadas a `_log_audit` en operaciones relevantes (creación/actualización/estado/eliminación). 
- Se actualizaron `schemas.py` con los nuevos DTOs para inventarios y auditoría, se agregaron tests de integración básicos en `backend/tests/stock/test_inventory_counts.py`, y se actualizaron los tipos y funciones del cliente en `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` junto con nuevas páginas `InventoryCountsPage.tsx` y `AuditPage.tsx` y rutas UI en `App.tsx` y `AppShell.tsx`. 
- Se ajustaron `TYPE_CHECKING` imports en `user.py` y otros archivos para evitar ciclos de importación. 

### Testing
- Intenté validar que la aplicación se pueda inicializar con `python -c "from app.main import create_app; create_app()"`, pero la comprobación falló por una incompatibilidad de `pyenv` en el entorno (`pyenv: version '3.12.3' is not installed`), por lo que no se pudo completar la inicialización automática. 
- No se ejecutó `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` ni la suite de `pytest` en este entorno de rollout por la misma restricción de versión de Python. 
- No se detectaron errores sintácticos en los cambios aplicados y las modificaciones buscan resolver la ambigüedad de FK que provocaba el error en tiempo de mapeo de SQLAlchemy.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve matching consistency between the browse UI and analyzer by normalizing goal/system taxonomy and aliases. 
- Make recommendations more context-aware and safer by adding query context, safety screening against meds/conditions, and evidence-weighted scoring. 
- Enable longitudinal personalization by adding simple daily tracking and using logs to adjust recommendation relevance. 

### Description
- Add canonical taxonomy aliases and new goal categories in `src/constants/taxonomy.ts` and introduce `normalizeGoals`/`normalizeSystems` in `src/utils/normalization.ts` to standardize goal/system matching. 
- Enhance analyzer (`src/utils/analyzer.ts`) with improved tokenization/stemming, weighted exact/partial/semantic matching, per-goal evidence multipliers, query context extraction (avoid stimulants/sedatives/etc.), safety assessment against `healthConditions`/`medications`, tracking-based score adjustments, and a diversity-aware recommendation selector. 
- Extend types in `src/types/index.ts` to carry `goalEvidence`, `safetyFlags`, and `cautionLevel` through recommendation objects. 
- Update browse UX (`src/components/AdvancedBrowse.tsx`) to use normalized goals/systems, refreshed goal categories, and more robust quick filters and similarity matching. 
- Expand main app (`src/App.tsx`) to capture additional profile fields (caffeine, budget, form preference, current supplements, conditions, medications), add a `Track` tab with daily logs persisted to localStorage, pass `trackingData` into `analyzeGoal`, and surface `safetyFlags`/`cautionLevel` on recommendation cards. 

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` and confirmed the app loaded successfully. 
- Ran an automated Playwright smoke script that opened the app, clicked the `📈 Track` tab, and captured a screenshot (`artifacts/tracking.png`), which completed successfully.

# Note

This is PR https://github.com/JCSDA/spack-stack/pull/1877 which was accidentally closed. See https://github.com/JCSDA/spack-stack/pull/1877 for the same information as below and for approvals.

## Description

This PR updates the spack submodule branch `spack-stack-dev` from the upstream spack `develop`. Until now, it was based on Spack v1.0.1. See https://github.com/JCSDA/spack/pull/574

This update requires us to switch to the new (spack v1) syntax for declaring preferred compilers, since the blanket `packages:all:require:['gcc']` (for example) no longer works for packages that don't depend on a compiler (no c, cxx, fortran dependency). While updating the common `packages_<compiler>.yaml` files, I removed the remaining `configs/common/packages_<compiler>.yaml.NOTYETUPDATED` files.

The concretizer now behaves slightly differently, and we can no longer declare external compiler runtime libraries. I opposed this for a long time, but, alas, I'll choose a different hill to die on. This had to be done for every site config. A few more tweaks to the common `packages.yaml` are needed to avoid duplicate packages. Note also that external packages now have to match any variants that are `require:`d in the environment config.

The above changes require updates to the `setup-meta-modules` extension, the GitHub actions workflows, and the unit tests for the spack-stack extension.

Lastly, this PR brings in a new version of bufr-query 0.0.5. Note that the concretizer in spack v1.0.1 had a bug that caused it to simply ignore bufr-query, even though it was supposed to be built (variant in jedi-base-env had default value `True`). The new concretizer fixed this bug, and now we do get `bufr-query` as part of the unified environment and the Skylab environment.

## Summary

- Implements Phase 1 of visual fallback design: screenshot + metadata when accessibility fails
- Adds new `visual-snapshot` operation for explicit visual mode
- Adds YAML config via `REPLICANT_CONFIG` environment variable
- Updates `find` operation to auto-include visual fallback when no results found

## Changes

### New Features
- **`visual-snapshot` operation**: Returns screenshot path, screen metadata (width, height, density), and current app info (package, activity)
- **Visual fallback on `find`**: When accessibility and OCR both find nothing, includes screenshot + metadata so LLM can estimate tap coordinates
- **YAML configuration**: Control visual fallback behavior per-project:
  ```yaml
  ui:
    visualModePackages: [com.problematic.app]  # Skip accessibility for these
    autoFallbackScreenshot: true                # Include screenshot on empty results
    includeBase64: false                        # Optionally include base64 data
  ```

### New Files
- `src/types/config.ts` - Config types and defaults
- `src/services/config.ts` - YAML loading and ConfigManager
- `tests/services/config.test.ts` - 9 tests for config loading
- `tests/integration/visual-fallback.test.ts` - 7 tests for visual fallback

### Modified Files
- `src/adapters/ui-automator.ts` - Added `getScreenMetadata()`, `getCurrentApp()`, `visualSnapshot()`
- `src/tools/ui.ts` - Added `visual-snapshot` operation, config-aware find
- `src/server.ts` - ConfigManager integration, loads config on startup

author: lyndonkl
body:
## Summary
- Add `--prefetch-factor` CLI argument to train.py (default: 2)
- Pass prefetch_factor to both `create_dataloaders` and `create_dataloaders_distributed`
- Each worker prefetches this many batches ahead, keeping GPU fed with data

## Recommended Settings
With your RunPod setup (128 vCPUs, 6x RTX 4090):
```bash
--num-workers 16 --prefetch-factor 4
```

This gives 16 workers × 4 prefetch = 64 batches queued per GPU, which should eliminate the "jumpy" progress bar caused by data loading bottleneck.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run training with `--num-workers 16 --prefetch-factor 4`
- [ ] Verify smoother progress bar (less jumping)
- [ ] Monitor CPU usage to ensure workers are utilized

### Summary
This pull request refactors all string filtering logic in the Catalog microservice to use MongoDB collation for case-insensitive queries, replacing the previous .ToLower() approach.
The change improves query performance, ensures index compatibility, and provides consistent case-insensitive behavior across all product lookups.

### Changes
Removed all `.ToLower()` usage in repository filters.
Introduced a centralized `_caseInsensitiveCollation` for reuse.
### Updated:
`GetProductsByName()`
`GetProductsByBrand()`
`GetProducts()` (search filter)
`DataFilter()` (sorting and paging)
Replaced substring searches with case-insensitive regex ("i" flag).
Ensured compatibility with future collation-aware indexes (to be added later).

### Benefits
Case-insensitive equality without client-side transformations.
Prepares for future index optimization (O(log n) lookups).
More consistent, maintainable query logic.
Cleaner, fully server-side query processing.
Type: `refactor`
Scope: `catalog`
Branch: `refactor/catalog-collation-case-insensitive-queries`

author: swenson
body:
This is a one-shot, ROM-only command meant to make some Device Ownership Transfer-like flows easier from MCU ROM or the SoC manager.

For example, if MCU has something like a Vendor PK hash burned into fuses and needs to match an ECDSA or MLDSA public key against it as part of DOT recovery, then it would need a way in the MCU ROM to compute SHA384/512 hashes, either using Caliptra or with a hardware or software SHA capability in MCU. Since Caliptra is meant to be the only cryptography capabilities for MCU, this means we need at least a simple SHA command offered by Caliptra ROM.

(This could potentially be worked around by using the existing CM_HMAC, and having something similar to a Vendor PK hash using HMACs, but this is cumbersome and would need to be computed per-device, since the only HMAC keys available to Caliptra ROM are stable keys, which are device-specific.)

Note: this supports computing the SHA of the entire mailbox contents (minus the command head), so can also be used for stashing.

This is targeted for 2.1 and 2.0.1 ROMs.

(Cherry picked and adapted from #3097)

author: nrayamajhee
body: Goal: Prevent public access to images and restrict viewing to authorized users only. 1. Backend Implementation (api) We will shift from direct S3 downloads to an API proxy model. - Modify api/src/photo.rs: - Uploads: Update the upload function to remove ObjectCannedAcl::PublicRead. New files will be private by default. - New Endpoint (view): Create a new handler pub async fn view(...). - Path: /photos/:name/view - Security: Validate the requesting user via ClerkJwt. - Authorization: Query the database (SELECT * FROM photo WHERE name = AND author_id = ) to ensure the user owns the photo. - Retrieval: Use aws_sdk_s3 to get_object from the bucket. - Response: Stream the S3 byte stream directly to the client with the correct Content-Type and Cache-Control headers. - Modify api/src/main.rs: - Register the new route: .route("/photos/:name/view", get(photo::view)) 2. Frontend Implementation (web) Since standard tags cannot send Authorization headers, we need a custom component to fetch images securely. - Create web/app/components/SecureImage.tsx: - A wrapper component that accepts a photoName and className. - Uses fetch() with the Authorization: Bearer header to call the new API endpoint. - Converts the response Blob into a local object URL (URL.createObjectURL). - Renders a standard tag using the secure object URL. - Update web/app/pages/photos.tsx: - Replace the direct usage of import.meta.env.VITE_R2_URL with the new component. 3. Migration (Self-Healing) - Existing images on S3/R2 will remain "Public" until manually updated, but the frontend will stop using the public URLs immediately. - Ideally, we would run a script to remove the Public ACL from existing objects, but strictly speaking, the API proxy will work regardless of the object's ACL status. 4. Trade-offs - Pros: Strict security (database-backed ownership checks), no exposed public URLs. - Cons: Higher bandwidth/CPU on the API server compared to direct S3 downloads.

author: tinogo
body:
Version 1.5.0 of the ucapi-framework introduced the attribute filtering logic (resp. change detection, so that no unnecessary changes get published to the remote), which works really great.

But there seems to be a small catch:
1. Entity-Attributes-Update will be ignored by the `ucapi`, as long as an entity is available (i.e. NOT configured)
2. `Device.get_device_attributes()` gets still called within `refresh_entity_state` --> that's good! :)
3. If there is an Entity which is based on the newly introduced ucapi-framework-Entity-ABC, these attributes will flow through `entity.update()` resp. `entity.update_attributes()`, which ultimately call `entity.filter_changed_attributes`

This can be problematic for devices which take some time to be "fully operational" (e.g. for devices where the `sound_mode_list` is static` but the `source_list` dynamic, this):
1. There the `sound_mode_list` "change" gets emitted as part of the initial Device-Update-Event, where the entity is still only "available"
2. When configuring such an entity (because of the now established device connection), only the `source_list` gets transferred again to the Remote, leaving the `sound_mode_list` empty.

This PR changes the `BaseIntegrationDriver.refresh_entity_state()`-method in a way, so that it doesn't do the entity-attribute-filtering.

body:
## Summary

     Major enhancement to the Copilot MCP Server adding production-grade reliability, security, and observability. This
    PR consolidates multiple improvements developed incrementally.

     ## Changes

     ### 🔐 Security
     - **Prompt via stdin instead of argv** — Prompts no longer visible in `ps`/`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (#11)
     - **Remove `shell: true`** — Eliminates shell injection risks (#9)
     - **Prompt size guard** — Configurable `COPILOT_MAX_PROMPT_BYTES` limit (default 24KB) (#10)
     - **Stdin error handling** — Gracefully handles EPIPE when CLI exits early

     ### 🚀 Reliability
     - **Remove hardcoded model allowlist** — `z.enum` replaced with `z.string()`, supports all 14+ models (#1)
     - **Non-interactive CLI mode** — Uses `--silent` + stdin instead of fragile timing-based `/exit` (#1)
     - **Resilient directory init** — `initDirectories()` warns instead of crashing on permission errors

     ### 📊 Observability
     - **Structured tool output** — `structuredContent` with model, durationMs, exitCode, stderrSnippet (#6)
     - **Leveled logging** — debug/info/warn/error with `COPILOT_LOG_LEVEL` control
     - **Optional file logging** — `COPILOT_LOG_FILE` for production debugging

     ### ⚙️ Configuration
     - **`COPILOT_MODEL`** — Default model selection
     - **`COPILOT_TIMEOUT`** — Command timeout in ms (default 60s)
     - **`COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL_TOOLS`** — Auto-approve tools (default false)
     - **`COPILOT_DEBUG`** — Enable debug logging
     - **`COPILOT_MAX_PROMPT_BYTES`** — Prompt size limit (0 = unlimited)

     ### 🔧 New Tool
     - **`copilot-list-models`** — Lists available models by parsing `copilot --help` with fallback list

     ## Breaking Changes

     None — all changes are backward compatible.

     ## Testing

     - Type-checks pass
     - Build succeeds (ESM + CJS)
     - End-to-end tested with Copilot CLI v0.0.388

     ## Environment Variables Reference

     | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
     |----------|------|---------|-------------|

     | `COPILOT_TIMEOUT` | number | 60000 | Timeout (ms) |

author: antoniosarosi
body:
## Summary

- Add `unsafe` change detection flag in CI workflow that triggers when `bex_heap/**` changes
- Add `miri-tests` job that runs Miri on bex_heap when unsafe code changes
- Consolidate `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` in bex_engine, bex_vm with safety documentation
- Add Miri-targeted tests for GC and TLAB operations
- **Fix heap concurrent resize data race with ChunkedVec**
- **Use const generic for ChunkedVec chunk size (compile-time shift/AND optimization)**

## Data Race Fix

### The Problem

When one VM writes to an existing object via TLAB while another VM's TLAB allocation triggers `Vec::resize_with()`, the Vec may reallocate its backing storage, invalidating pointers held by the first VM. This was detected by Miri but only manifests as a race under specific timing conditions.

### The Solution

Replace `Vec<Object<F>>` with `ChunkedVec<Object<F>>` in `BexHeap::spaces`. ChunkedVec stores objects in fixed-size heap-allocated chunks. Growing the storage adds new chunks without moving existing data, ensuring pointer stability during concurrent access.

### Key Changes

- Add `chunked_vec.rs` with ChunkedVec data structure
- Update BexHeap to use ChunkedVec for runtime spaces
- Add `write_runtime_object()` and `get_runtime_object_mut()` APIs
- Update tlab.rs, gc.rs, and vm.rs to use new access patterns
- Enable Miri concurrent tests (remove `cfg_attr(miri, ignore)`)

### ChunkedVec Optimizations

- **Const generic chunk size**: `ChunkedVec<T, const CHUNK_SIZE: usize = 4096>` enables compile-time optimization of `index / CHUNK_SIZE` → right shift, `index % CHUNK_SIZE` → bitwise AND
- **Compile-time power-of-2 assertion**: Non-power-of-2 chunk sizes fail at compile time
- **Documented future optimization**: Virtual memory approach (mmap/VirtualAlloc) documented as potential future optimization for `base + offset` access pattern

### Miri Compatibility

✅ **Passes Miri with both stacked borrows (default) and tree borrows**

The ChunkedVec implementation uses raw pointer operations (`(*chunks_ptr).push(chunk)`) instead of method calls that would create `&mut Vec` borrows, avoiding conflicts with concurrent reads under stacked borrows.

### Memory Leak Fix

Fixed memory leak in `set()` and `push_with()` - previously these used `std::ptr::write` without dropping the old value. Now properly calls `std::ptr::drop_in_place` before writing.

## New Tests

| Test | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `test_miri_stack_forwarding_after_gc` | Simulates VM stack update after GC |
| `test_miri_deep_reference_chain_forwarding` | Tests nested object graph traversal |
| `test_miri_multiple_gc_cycles_with_changing_roots` | Tests root set evolution across GC cycles |
| `test_miri_tlab_invalidation_and_refill` | Tests TLAB invalidation and allocation after GC |
| `test_miri_set_object_mutation` | Tests unsafe `set_object` write path ✅ |
| `test_miri_concurrent_tlab_allocation` | Multi-threaded TLAB allocation ✅ |
| `test_miri_concurrent_tlab_refill` | Concurrent TLAB chunk exhaustion/refill ✅ |

## Test plan

- [x] All 48 bex_heap tests pass normally
- [x] All 48 tests pass under Miri with stacked borrows (default) (~3.5 min)
- [x] All 48 tests pass under Miri with tree borrows
- [x] No memory leaks detected by Miri
- [x] Concurrent tests enabled and passing
- [ ] CI Miri job runs and passes

주최사 공연 등록 API를 연동합니다.

## 📚 Tasks

- 공연 등록 POST API 연동
- FormData 변환 유틸 추가 
- 서버 스펙에 맞는 serialize 직렬화 함수 추가
- instance.ts에 인터셉터 추가

## 🔍 Describe
- `to-form-data.ts` : `Record<string, string | Blob>` 형태를 FormData로 변환하는 유틸 (append 공통 처리)
- `serialize-event-form.ts` : 폼 입력값을 서버 요청 스펙에 맞게 FormData로 직렬화

데이터 흐름은 다음과 같습니다. 똑같은 폼 뷰에서 수정, 삭제, 추가 API가 붙어야 하기 때문에 반복 코드를 줄이고자 event-form을 widgets에 분리했어요.
1. 폼 입력
2. 제출 버튼 클릭 시 EventForm이 onSubmit(values)로 제출값 전달
3. 페이지에서 serializeCreateFestivalFormData(values)로 FormData 생성
4. useMutaion으로 POST 호출
5. 성공/실패 처리

추가로, host에서 401 권한 에러가 뜨는 문제가 있었는데 instance.ts에 인터셉터를 추가해 해결했습니다.
